newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MARSEILLE PRESIDENT PLEDGES FUTURE TO CLUB.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARSEILLE PRESIDENT PLEDGES FUTURE TO CLUB.

text.p: Marseille president Robert Louis-Dreyfus vowed on Monday to pour money into the French club next season and described rumours he would quit as "pure fantasy".
The former European champions have virtually given up on their pre-season target of a UEFA Cup place. Newly-promoted to the first division, they are currently 11th after four successive defeats.
"In 25 years in business I have never left (a job) on a losing note," said Louis-Dreyfus, head of the Adidas sports equipment company. "Marseille will be no different."
Calling rumours of his departure "pure fantasy", he vowed to invest 150 million francs ($26.3 million) into the club.
And he confirmed coach Gerard Gili will remain in charge until the end of the season.
"Then we'll look at the positive and negative aspects and draw our conclusions. We have big projects for the future," said the president.
Louis-Dreyfus said Marseille would strengthen their squad with six or seven new players, including one or two top strikers, next season with a view to finishing among the top five.
"If we don't get into Europe next year you can say I've failed," he concluded.
